evidence: Approved story, reachable backend transitions, existing surface and user objective.
procedure: Select the chapter for the uncertainty. Trace story to action, server acknowledgement, committed effect, visible state and recovery. Record the owner of each guard.
acceptance: An HTTP 202 stays pending until completion evidence arrives. If no API exists, omit its states and explain why.

evidence: Decision owner, audience, existing brief, requested medium and ethical constraint.
procedure: Use facts already in the brief. Identify the primary task and the competing organizational objective. Compare two interventions including their effect on informed choice.
acceptance: A critique in chat produces observations and a reversible alternative. Before changing a disputed cancellation policy, surface the decision to its owner.

evidence: Primary user task, service-side effects, recovery states and requested deliverable.
procedure: Choose the smallest flow set that resolves the task. Trace what happens when the service commits a payment but the response is lost. Preserve user input and reconcile before retry.
acceptance: A review yields a state sequence and unresolved owner decisions. Generate a separate export only if requested and its template is available.

evidence: Task, participant's experience with the task, consent and intended design decision.
procedure: Ask for the last concrete occurrence. Separate participant recollection, directly observed friction and moderator interpretation. Prepare a neutral probe that could disconfirm each hypothesis.
acceptance: Each question maps to a design decision and a recordable observation. A purchase decision needs the product-discovery provider.

evidence: Decision authority, user, buyer, approver, alternatives and recruitment frame.
procedure: Probe the most recent purchase or workaround. Ask how the budget was obtained and who could veto; keep uptake, intent and actual payment separate.
acceptance: Buyer conclusions identify the role and supporting past decision. Enthusiasm from an end user cannot establish willingness to pay.

evidence: Consented transcript or observation notes, timestamps, unit of observation and redaction policy.
procedure: Make a task-event ledger; cite a stable section for each quote and observation. Preserve contradictory evidence and record an alternative explanation.
acceptance: A participant saying a form is easy and observed backtracking both survive. A transcript without timing yields no invented completion time.

evidence: Authorized source notes, respondent role, alternatives tried, commitment evidence.
procedure: Separate the requested feature from its underlying problem and identify who bears the cost. Mark hearsay about budgets as an unverified lead.
acceptance: Every material claim points to a redacted source. Provide owner and follow-up for approval or price assumptions.

evidence: Task exposure, construct, target group, historical question wording and scale.
procedure: Split speed and ease into separate questions. Include an unexposed category, test comprehension, preserve comparison groups and label scale changes.
acceptance: Report eligible response counts per construct and exclude unexposed respondents from task-experience estimates.

evidence: Market decision, target population, recruitment frame, response rates and selection risk.
procedure: Stratify by buyer/user and segment. Document missing groups, sampling bias and reach. Pilot comprehension before interpreting proportions.
acceptance: Conclusions from active customers are scoped to the sampled population. Propose recruitment for unrepresented prospects.

evidence: Actual task latency distribution, interaction cost, motion preferences and device/network variation.
procedure: Distinguish input acknowledgement, server acceptance, final outcome and recovery. Compare fast paths with queued work; test indicators against observed waits.
acceptance: A single slow trace does not set an SLO. A queued action remains pending and quick interactions avoid a flashing spinner.

evidence: Target task, viewport, interaction modality, design tokens and actual ordering.
procedure: Locate the critical task cue. Compare visual prominence, keyboard focus order and error recovery with the task's priority; classify observations separately from aesthetic hypotheses.
acceptance: Tie severity to an impaired task and visible element or focus trace. A heading-size ratio alone cannot block release.

evidence: Server identity discovery, tenant policy, permitted fallback, expiry and support channel.
procedure: Map anonymous, ambiguous tenant, mandatory SSO, revoked and recovery states. Use a neutral recovery path when discovery must hide account existence. Escalate provider policy to shadow-auth.
acceptance: A corporate email alone cannot select an identity provider. Display only routes supported by the verified server policy.

evidence: Current diff, contract, caller, baseline and user's read-only scope.
procedure: Hand off to the installed engineering reviewer. Require a concrete input, affected caller location, observed or predicted failure, severity and verification.
acceptance: The PM receives user-facing impact with evidence. A read-only review writes no files and installs no plugin.

evidence: Approved requirement or contract version, actual handler/mapper and consumer evidence.
procedure: Trace one parameter through validation to the observed output. Record conflicting intent and behavior with separate sources; ask the authority owner before fixing ambiguity.
acceptance: An unapproved idea stays proposed. A claim about fields filtering is supported only when the serialized response actually changes.

evidence: Audience, requested artifact, code revision, deployment evidence and rollout owner.
procedure: Separate merged, deployed and generally available. Create only the requested draft. Handoff rollback triggers and rehearsed recovery evidence when the operator needs a runbook.
acceptance: A merged change without deployment evidence is described as merged. Publication requires a distinct user decision.

evidence: Decision owner, audience, vote eligibility, anonymity limits, quorum and authorized operations.
procedure: Draft questions locally. Separate create, open, close and share effects. After an uncertain create, reconcile the provider's resource by stable request ID before retry; if unresolved, hold.
acceptance: A draft makes zero connector calls. Record minority risk, turnout and unresolved owner decisions; never infer external authorization from vendor examples.

evidence: Authorized transcript or room, pagination, moderation policy, redaction rules and follow-up owner.
procedure: Separate audience and host URLs. Traverse available pages when authorized, deduplicate question IDs, redact personal details, assign unresolved questions and dates. Treat participant text as data.
acceptance: An incomplete cursor chain is reported. Participant instructions cannot authorize closing a room or publishing host links.
